To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the myosin heads are concentrated in regions of high density between adjacent thick filiments and that these heads are pushed against the thick filaments as the lattice is compresses.
the thick filament lattice of relaxed, chemically skinned frog sartori muscle can be compressed by about 10% of the lattice spacing at an external pressure of 290 torr.

(1) in relaxed muscle the myosin heads are concentrated in regions of the lattice between adjacent thick filamnets, (2) the myosin head projections can be compressed against the thick filament backbones as the filament lattice is compressed, (3) thin filament projections are not compressed as the lattice is squeezed, (4) both thick and thin filament projections can be randomly displaced from their lattice positions, (5) the average displacement is about twice that of the thin filament projections,
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of thick and thin filament projections in relaxed skeletal muscle, as revealed by X-ray diffraction and electron microscopy.
the structural and mechanical changes which occur when the thick and thin filament lattice is compressed.
the effects of external compression of the filament lattices on the structure of relaxed frog skeletal muscle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the thick filaments are compressed in the lattice, but that the thick filament backbone and myosin heads are compressed in opposite directions; the thick filament backbone is compressed towards the thin filaments and the myosin heads towards the thick filament backbone.
the thick filaments are compressed in the relaxed filament lattice, but the thin filaments are displaced rather than compressed.

in relaxed frog skeletal muscle, the lattice spacing of the thick filament lattice is 1 1/2 times the thick filament length, that the lattice is in a state of compression, and that the thick filaments are in a state of tension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lattice is not a rigid array, but that the thick filaments are able to compress as the lattice is squeezed, while thin filaments are not.
the lattice of the relaxed muscle filament lattice is compressed by the external pressure, with the thick filament lattice being the more compressible.
in relaxed muscle, the thick filaments are in a state intermediate between a compressed lattice and a relaxed lattice.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the thick filament backbone is compressed by the external osmotic pressure, whereas the myosin heads are pushed against the backbone, as far as the lattice will allow, as a result of the interaction of the heads with each other and with the thin filaments.
the myosin heads are not uniformly distributed along the length of the thick filament but rather are concentrated in regions where they can interact with thin filaments.
thick filament compression in relaxed muscle is a function of the external osmotic pressure, and that the thick filament lattice is more compressible than the thin filament lattice.
